title: Book of Mormon Timeline

sections.label: Jerusalem & the early record
sections.hint: Lehi’s departure sits in Judah’s last decades—use the backdrop lane to keep Jeremiah and Babylon in view.

sections.label: The Mosiah knot (parallel lanes)
sections.hint: Printed order flashbacks. Zeniff/Limhi and Alma₁ overlap Mosiah₂ in Zarahemla until they merge.

sections.label: After the merge → Christ
sections.hint: Mostly linear. War years in Alma are skipped on purpose.

sections.label: Closing the record
sections.hint: Mormon abridges; Moroni finishes; Ether is a jump to an earlier people.

sources: Book of Mormon internal chronology (chapter headings / Institute manuals)
OT backdrop aligned with Bible Timeline (Jeremiah, Babylonian waves, 586)

entities.label: Josiah’s reforms
entities.whyConfusing: Not in the Book of Mormon text—backdrop for the world Lehi is born into.
entities.summary: Covenant renewal and temple-centered reform in Judah set the religious climate a generation before Lehi’s call.

entities.label: Deuteronomic reform climate
entities.whyConfusing: A modern label for the reform movement—not a Book of Mormon book. One lens for “centralize worship, keep the covenant.”
entities.summary: Reform energy around law, covenant, and exclusive loyalty to the Lord—helpful context for prophets confronting Jerusalem’s politics.

entities.label: Jeremiah in Jerusalem
entities.whyConfusing: Jeremiah and Lehi overlap in the same crisis city; the Book of Mormon starts mid-stream in that story.
entities.summary: Prophet warning Judah as Babylon rises—same decades as Lehi’s ministry in Jerusalem.

entities.label: Babylon — first wave
entities.whyConfusing: First pressure/deportation wave—not yet the final destruction.

otParallel.label: Open OT Timeline: Fall of Jerusalem

entities.summary: Babylon asserts control; early captives and tribute begin the unraveling of Judah.

entities.label: Babylon — second wave
entities.whyConfusing: Jehoiachin’s deportation wave—still before the 586 temple destruction.

otParallel.label: Open OT Timeline: Fall of Jerusalem

entities.summary: Major deportation including the king and elites; Jerusalem limps on under Zedekiah.

entities.label: Lehi leaves Jerusalem
entities.whyConfusing: Sync point: Nephite story starts while Judah’s crisis is still unfolding.
entities.summary: Lehi prophesies and flees with his family into the wilderness as Babylon tightens its grip.

entities.label: Fall of Jerusalem (586)
entities.bookRef: OT · cf. 2 Nephi 1 (news reaches Lehi’s family later)
entities.whyConfusing: Happens after Lehi has already left; the family hears of destruction later.

otParallel.label: Open OT Timeline: Fall of Jerusalem

entities.summary: Temple destroyed, monarchy ended—the catastrophe Jeremiah foresaw and Lehi escaped.

entities.label: Nephi’s record (to the land of promise)
entities.whyConfusing: Mostly linear. Keep Jerusalem’s fall in the backdrop, not as the next Nephite chapter.
entities.summary: Journey, ship, arrival, teaching, and the small plates’ early testimony.

entities.label: Jacob → Enos → Omni
entities.whyConfusing: Centuries pass quickly on short books—Omni is a bridge of record keepers.
entities.summary: Small plates continue through priests and kings until Mosiah₁ leads a party to Zarahemla.

entities.label: Mosiah₁ finds Zarahemla
entities.whyConfusing: Sync point: Nephites meet Mulekites; later flashbacks happen under this united people.
entities.summary: Northern migrants join the people of Zarahemla—stage set for Benjamin and Mosiah₂.

entities.label: Words of Mormon (editorial bridge)
entities.whyConfusing: Mormon explains why the small plates sit where they do—not a new generation of story.
entities.summary: Editor’s hinge between the small plates and the large-plate abridgment beginning in Mosiah.

entities.label: Benjamin’s speech
entities.whyConfusing: Main lane in Zarahemla. The Zeniff flashback (printed next) already overlaps this era.
entities.summary: King Benjamin teaches and names Mosiah₂—while a separate Nephite colony story is about to be told out of order.

entities.label: Mosiah₂ reigns in Zarahemla
entities.whyConfusing: While Mosiah₂ rules, the book digresses into Limhi and Alma—those stories are concurrent, not sequels.
entities.summary: Zarahemla’s king sends a search party, then later receives Limhi’s and Alma’s peoples.

entities.label: Zeniff returns to Nephi’s land
entities.whyConfusing: Flashback: starts generations before Benjamin’s speech even though you read it after.
entities.summary: A Nephite group re-settles the land of Nephi among the Lamanites—parallel history.

entities.label: Noah’s wicked reign · Abinadi
entities.whyConfusing: Still the colony lane—Abinadi’s martyrdom sets up Alma₁, not the next Zarahemla chapter.
entities.summary: Noah rejects Abinadi; Alma₁ believes and will flee—while Zarahemla has its own kings.

entities.label: Limhi’s people in bondage
entities.whyConfusing: Concurrent with Alma₁ in the wilderness—not a story that finishes before Alma begins.
entities.summary: Limhi’s remnant suffers under Lamanite rule until Ammon from Zarahemla helps them escape.

entities.label: Alma₁ at the waters of Mormon
entities.whyConfusing: Printed after Limhi, but overlapping Limhi—Alma’s people are a third concurrent thread.
entities.summary: Alma₁ flees Noah, baptizes at Mormon, builds a church in the wilderness, then also reaches Zarahemla.

entities.label: Limhi + Alma join Mosiah₂
entities.whyConfusing: The knot resolves: three lanes become one people again in Zarahemla.
entities.summary: Limhi’s group and Alma’s group arrive; Mosiah₂ authorizes churches—flashbacks catch up to the main clock.

entities.label: Reign of the judges begins
entities.whyConfusing: Back to a single main lane—Alma the Younger becomes chief judge/high priest.
entities.summary: Monarchy ends; Alma₂ leads as the book of Alma opens.

entities.label: Alma₂ — missions & wars (compressed)
entities.whyConfusing: V1 skips year-by-year wars on purpose—the narrative stays one lane.
entities.summary: Missions, dissent, and warfare. Use chapter headings when you need a battle year; this card is only a bridge.

entities.label: Helaman → 3 Nephi (before Christ)
entities.whyConfusing: Linear countdown to the sign of Christ’s birth and the destruction before his visit.
entities.summary: Pride cycles, Gadianton robbers, and signs—still one main timeline.

entities.label: Christ visits the Nephites
entities.whyConfusing: Major sync point—ministry in the Americas after the crucifixion.
entities.summary: The risen Christ teaches, heals, and establishes his church among the people.

entities.label: 4 Nephi — Zion, then decline
entities.whyConfusing: Centuries in one short book—peace first, then division returns.
entities.summary: Generations of unity erode into tribal conflict again.

entities.label: Mormon’s abridgment & wars
entities.whyConfusing: Mormon is both editor of earlier plates and a character in the final wars.
entities.summary: Final Nephite–Lamanite conflicts culminating toward Cumorah.

entities.label: Moroni finishes the record
entities.whyConfusing: Moroni also inserts Ether—jumping to a much earlier people before his farewell.
entities.summary: Last Nephite prophet seals the record and speaks to latter-day readers.

entities.label: Ether — Jaredite record (earlier spur)
entities.whyConfusing: Not “after” Mormon in real time—an ancient civilization abridged and placed near the end of the volume.
entities.summary: Jaredite rise and fall. Read it as a side track that ends before (and warns) the Nephite story.
